question:
Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All keys are locks.

All locks are handles.

Conclusions:

I. Some locks are keys.

II. All handles are keys.
options:
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

Only conclusion I follows

Only conclusion II follows

Both conclusions I and II follow
solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. Only conclusion I follows.

Conclusion:

I. Some locks are keys - Follows (As All keys are locks so some locks are also keys)

II. All handles are keys - Does not follow (As All keys are locks and all locks are handles so some handles can be keys it is definite but all handles are keys it is false)

question:

Statements:

Some pens are books.

All books are cars.

Some cars are spoons.

Conclusions:

(I): Some spoons are pens.

(II): Some books are pens
options:
Only conclusion (I) follows

Only conclusion (II) follows

Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow

Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows
solution:

(I) Some spoons are pens - Does not follow (As there is no definite relation between pens and spoons so, it does not follow)

Thus, Only conclusion (II) follows.
